scope: Adapter TagDuel clássico 2v2 isolado para Curse of Darkness: dano obrigatório de 1000 LP somente após resolução da Carta de Magia; distinção entre ativação negada e efeito negado; roteamento pelo assento físico que ativou a Magia; múltiplas cópias, negação contínua, idempotência, integridade de UID e inventário imutável.

cards.name: Curse of Darkness
cards.officialEffect: Each time a Spell Card is activated, immediately after it resolves, the player that activated it takes 1000 damage.

design.resolution: Only a Spell whose activation resolved triggers the Trap. A Spell whose effect was negated but whose activation resolved still triggers; a negated activation does not.
design.routing: The damaged team is derived from the physical seat that activated the Spell, never from the Spell's immutable owner UID or the Trap's controller.
design.stacking: Each face-up, resolved, non-negated copy creates a separate 1000 LP plan. Plans are deterministic by source UID and clamp at remaining LP.
design.negation: Jinzo blocks Trap activations and Royal Decree negates Trap effects; both suppress Curse of Darkness. Per-source negation is also accepted.
design.integrity: Event IDs are fingerprinted against the resolved Spell and active sources. Replays are idempotent; changed facts under the same ID are rejected. The adapter returns plans only and never mutates LP, Decks, hands, zones or inventory.
design.admission: The card is absent from the shared catalog and certification source. Tests use already-enabled Trap IDs as isolated fixture aliases; this does not admit or certify Curse of Darkness.

tests: Resolved Spell damage and both-team routing
Physical Spell owner versus active teammate actor
No source, face-down/unresolved source and per-source negation
Multiple copies, cross-team controllers, deterministic stacking and lethal LP clamp
Real Spell identity, physical UID, active-seat authorization and stale LP
Idempotent replay, changed-fact replay rejection and malformed ledger
Duplicate source UID rejection, immutability and owner-rule invariants
